items.reason: Artifacts assigns exploration its own type, ordered after spec and before progress.
Dashboard artifacts use the same ordered artifact list.
The orphan-markdown validator explicitly exempts exploration.md.
Other manifest validation and orphan-markdown rejection remain intact.
ExploreRequested reads the set-level explore boolean beside existing phase accessors.
Only explicit true enables automatic exploration; absent and false do not.
ExplorerOverride reads agents and effort through the shared AgentDirective type.
The authoring guide documents both keys and their participation polarity.
The guide states the shared-seam and dependent-later-task rule.
Shared constants supply names, and a guide-to-manifest test checks agreement.
The explore command invokes a fresh agent with manifest listing, task bodies, and optional spec.
The explorer template requests all five specified areas of code orientation.
The template requires path-or-symbol claims, about one page, and the observed branch and commit.
The prescribed report sections contain no prior-art section or request.
Successful passes atomically overwrite exploration.md directly in the set directory.
Exploration has its own captured-run phase, spend bucket, and retry-cap phase.
Manual exploration bypasses both the manifest participation key and machine enable switch.
Failed, timed-out, and interrupted runs return before replacing the report.
Integration tests invoke exploreResolvedSet directly; none covers the command through reply, report, and captured run together.
Implement prompts conditionally include the existing report’s path and explanation.
Implement prompt construction checks existence and carries only the path, never report contents.
The prompt limits edits to lines this attempt falsified and forbids other changes.
The edit boundary explicitly permits the exploration report beside the task file.
The existing “Before you hand-write mechanism” block remains unchanged.
Assist prompts place the exploration pointer beside refinement context and recent progress.
Implement and assist goldens cover report-present and report-absent cases.
The drain invokes explorePhase before its first task selection.
An existing report bypasses exploration without invoking an agent.
Undeclared sets bypass the automatic exploration phase.
The independent work.explore group defaults enabled when its group or key is absent.
Disabling automatic exploration suppresses drain passes while manual exploration remains available.
Explorer resolution applies CLI, manifest, and configuration precedence independently to agents and effort.
Human-completed sets bypass the drain’s exploration phase.
Report reuse depends on presence, with no comparison against the checkout’s tree.
Whole-drain tests assert exploration runs before tasks when absent and never runs when present.
The shared fallback walk retries exploration using the standard per-phase cap and delays.
Failed captured exploration without a report derives EXPLORE-FAILED and stops draining.
Parking derives from captured-run metadata and report absence without schema additions.
EXPLORE-FAILED is distinct from BLOCKED and preserves its existing meaning.
Ready-set selectors and daemon selection exclude rows carrying EXPLORE-FAILED.
attendableHITLTaskSets ignores row status, so a parked set with an eligible HITL task remains selectable.
Exhausting a parkable pass appends one set-level progress record naming exploration and its failure reason.
The skip-explore flag bypasses exploration and permits an explicitly selected parked set to drain.
Writing a report or withdrawing the declaration removes the derived park.
CONTEXT.md lists EXPLORE-FAILED among drain-stop and automatic-selection exclusions.
Unexplored sets carry a separate exploration mark and reason rendered beside status.
Undeclared sets resolve to an empty exploration mark.
Refresh resolves exploration once onto rows, which feed all four display surfaces.
ExploreMarkText explicitly returns empty for EXPLORE-FAILED, suppressing parked sets’ marks.
Dashboard detail renders a ReportPointer containing path and recorded SHA without report prose.
The sign-off preamble includes exploration immediately beside refinement.
Removing a successful report causes its completed captured run to derive failure, parking the set instead of re-exploring.

scores.rationale: Good reuse and broad coverage, but parking recovery, HITL selection, mark visibility, and command-level testing remain incomplete.
